evidence.reason: In the identity-less cleanup path, the code reads the derived scope and, when LoadState is not-found, skips the cgroup ownership check, then unconditionally runs systemctl stop. A scope with the same run-ID-derived name can be created by another state directory between the show and the stop, so cleanup can stop another run's guest. This bypasses the code's own ownership guard at lines 1573-1575. The smallest compatible fix is to skip the stop when before LoadState is not-found (and, if desired, require positive ownership before stopping an existing scope).
